title: Rebalancing two disjoint matchings
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $M$ and $N$ be two disjoint matchings of $G$ (each a set of edges, no two of which share a vertex) with $\abs{N} < \abs{M}$. Then there exist disjoint matchings $M'$ and $N'$ of $G$ such that $\abs{M'} = \abs{M} - 1$, $\abs{N'} = \abs{N} + 1$, and $M' \cup N' = M \cup N$.
replaced:
Let $M$ and $N$ be disjoint matchings of $G$ with $|M| > |N|$. Then there are disjoint
matchings $M'$ and $N'$ of $G$ such that $|M'| = |M| - 1$, $|N'| = |N| + 1$ and $M' \cup
N' = M \cup N$.
